clue.text: Pinnacle gives elevated impression on paper

parts.note: elevated means high, raised up
a watermark is the faint design pressed into paper during manufacture

explanation.surface: A summit offers a raised mark embossed on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point reached on a scale of achievement is a peak or pinnacle, named after the line left by a flood tide.

clue.text: Heard of terrible mountains needed this to tackle them?

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters of 'Heard of' are mangled into a new order

parts.note: mountains are heights, lofty places

explanation.surface: A climber, having heard of fearsome peaks, wonders what nerve it takes to attempt them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges HEARD OF into HEADFOR; the definition leans on the whole clue, since 'them' refers back to the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone climbing peaks needs freedom from vertigo, a nerve for being up high.

clue.text: Russian writer's journey upset a king

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is the writer himself

parts.note: a go is a turn or trip, a journey

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: King Log is the wooden block sent as a king to the frogs in Aesop's fable

explanation.surface: A Russian author's travels are disturbed by a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a king' is King Log from Aesop: the frogs asked Zeus for a ruler and were sent a wooden block; 'upset' flips that block in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolai Gogol was the nineteenth-century novelist who wrote Dead Souls.

clue.text: He devised a type of bridge as he went to work

definitions.text: He devised a type of bridge

indicators.note: to work something is to knead and reshape it, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An engineer came up with a bridge design on his way to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges the ten letters of AS HE WENT TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Wheatstone popularised the bridge circuit for measuring electrical resistance that carries his name.

clue.text: Advertisement for a two-wheeler

explanation.surface: A poster promoting a bicycle or scooter.
explanation.definitionFit: A film preview advertising a coming release, and a small towed cart that often runs on just two wheels.

clue.text: Swimming in a circle, a fish

indicators.note: in places the fish inside the circle

parts.note: a ring is a circle
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish swims round and round in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: A head that is swimming is dizzy and spinning, staggering about.

clue.text: Sort of light getting hot in vault

parts.note: an arc light is a type of lamp
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A lamp heats up inside a vaulted cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: A vault is a curved roof structure, a span shaped like a bow.

clue.text: King spoiling fine advantage creates precarious situation

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: spoiling means the letters of 'fine' are ruined and jumbled

parts.note: an edge is an advantage

explanation.surface: A monarch wrecking a good lead lands himself in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A balance so fine that the outcome could go either way is a tense, perilous state.

clue.text: Test keynote for anthem

parts.note: a Test match is an international fixture in cricket or rugby
E is a musical note, a key

explanation.surface: Before a Test match the main note is struck for the national song.
explanation.definitionFit: The socialist song of the workers' movement was long sung as a political anthem.

clue.text: Boy breaks stone into lots of tiny ones

indicators.note: breaks means the boy's name bursts into the middle of the stone

parts.note: agate is a semi-precious stone
Greg is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad smashes a rock into many little pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravel or crushed rock mixed into concrete is a mass of small stones bound together.

clue.text: Corner source of gold to make money out of it

indicators.note: out of it means the money word sits outside the gold's letter

parts.note: to coin money is to mint it

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cornered prospector uses a gold strike to turn a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' gives G from gold, and COIN goes 'out of it', round it. This old spelling of 'quoin' is mainly met in Shakespeare's 'coign of vantage'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a projecting angle or cornerstone of a building, as in a vantage point.

clue.text: Service to be retaken, if first returned in the net

indicators.note: first places the turned-round word ahead of the service
returned means 'if' is sent back and read the other way

parts.note: in tennis a let is a serve that clipped the net and must be played again

explanation.surface: A tennis serve is replayed after it clipped the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns IF into FI, which comes 'first'.
explanation.definitionFit: A filet is a lace or mesh fabric, a kind of netting.

clue.text: Left to exhibit animals here

parts.note: to air something is to display it publicly

explanation.surface: A zoo is told to leave its creatures on show.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is where wild beasts live and shelter.

clue.text: Colour with fibre-tip — that's old advice

parts.note: red is a colour
the tip, the last letter, of the word fibre is E

explanation.surface: Someone recommends colouring in with a felt pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fibre-tip' looks like a felt pen; read it as the tip of the word 'fibre'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for counsel, a recommendation given.

clue.text: Footballers are rough folk

explanation.surface: Players of football are a coarse lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barbarians are a famous invitational rugby union club, and also uncivilised, savage people.

clue.text: Start to reprimand native soundly and bluster

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
soundly signals that the word is spoken and spelt differently

parts.note: a native is a British oyster bred in home waters, such as at Whitstable

explanation.surface: A local is firmly told off for shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like 'thoroughly'; here it means the oyster word is said aloud. A native is a British name for a farmed oyster.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily and swagger, behaving boisterously.

clue.text: Thought to be in teaching

parts.note: tuition is instruction, teaching

explanation.surface: An idea that is supposedly part of education.
explanation.definitionFit: An instinctive insight or hunch is a kind of thought reached without reasoning.

clue.text: Please note, boy has gone to study

parts.note: G is a musical note
a lad is a boy
a den is a private room for work, a study

explanation.surface: A request to note that a youngster has gone off to his room to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to delight or cheer them up.

clue.text: Put out, having no qualified claimant

explanation.surface: A title lapses, put out of use, with nobody entitled to inherit it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire that is quenched is dead, and a peerage with no surviving heir has died out.

clue.text: From motorists' auction, picked up vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means the run of letters is lifted and read upwards

parts.note: the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation
a mart is a market or auction

explanation.surface: A car is collected from a sale run by a drivers' club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns RACMART round. The RAC is a British breakdown and motoring club.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram carriage is a public passenger conveyance running on rails.

clue.text: Force to submit a theme

explanation.surface: Making someone yield is the topic under discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: To subdue a people is to bring them under control, and a topic is what a talk is about.

clue.text: Male children will receive money and gold, I'll warrant

indicators.note: will receive means the sons take the money inside them

parts.note: sons are male children
P is penny, a small coin
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Boys are promised cash and gold by a guarantor.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is what a backer says: one who vouches for another.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarantor who vouches for someone else is effectively saying they will answer for them.

clue.text: Cricket kit found by Glamorgan opener

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, like an opening batsman

parts.note: rig is gear, equipment

explanation.surface: Cricket gear is located beside Glamorgan's opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cricket' is the insect, not the sport; Glamorgan is a Welsh county cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: A grig is a dialect name for a small lively creature such as a grasshopper or the chirping insect.

clue.text: Pop round to see plinth

parts.note: pop is a familiar word for father
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Father drops by to look at a pedestal.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower part of a wall or the block of a pedestal between base and cornice.

clue.text: Run-away parson makes the front page

indicators.note: away means the run letter is taken out

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A clergyman who absconded is headline news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run-away' looks like an eloping priest; split it as Run (R) and 'away', removing one R from RECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The right-hand page of an open book, the front side of a leaf.

clue.text: In a predicament, taken up alcohol

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the letters are read going upwards
In means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone in a fix has taken to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points to REDIC inside 'predicament', and 'taken up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Fermented apple juice is an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Find regular place in radio programme for "In the Groove"

explanation.surface: A song finds its weekly spot on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheduled spot in broadcasting, and a narrow channel or slit.

clue.text: It is going to be poetic stuff

definitions.text: It is going to be poetic

explanation.surface: Verse is about to be made into cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic contraction of 'it will', and a woven fabric with diagonal ribs.

clue.text: Accountant's girl — she was incredible

parts.note: CA is chartered accountant, and the 's is kept as S
Sandra is a girl's name

explanation.surface: The bookkeeper's girlfriend was astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incredible' means not believed: the Trojan prophetess was cursed so no one would trust her prophecies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan seer was fated never to be believed, so she was literally not credited.

clue.text: Character takes book in park

parts.note: nature is someone's character
to reserve is to book in advance

explanation.surface: A personality brings a volume into the gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: A protected area for wildlife is a kind of country park.
